written.q: Describe the structure of the group project and the mandatory architecture requirements.
written.a: Seven weeks; eight teams of seven; two projects (Apartment Management, University Services) each built by four teams who own bounded microservices but are jointly responsible for the integrated product. Mandatory: independently deployable services with explicit owners, an API Gateway, a centralised JWT authentication service, one database or schema per service with no cross-service DB access, documented REST APIs with defined timeout and failure behaviour, consistent response conventions and centralised exception handling, Docker Compose for the full local system, health information and logs, versioned OpenAPI contracts and a shared modular React frontend.

written.q: Explain the cross-team governance rules and why they are needed.
written.a: A Project Integration Council of the four Team Leads meets weekly and records decisions, dependencies, interface changes, risks and owners. API contract changes must be announced before implementation and documented; nobody may silently change shared authentication, gateway routes, data definitions or response formats; shared frontend changes need reviewed PRs. They are needed because each team's services depend on others' APIs, and uncoordinated changes would break the integrated release (Conway's law: communication structure shapes the system).

written.q: Define the Definition of Ready and Definition of Done and write a user story with Given-When-Then acceptance criteria for a reservation.
written.a: Ready: clear purpose and value, testable criteria, dependencies and API assumptions identified, sufficient design, estimate and owner, fits the sprint. Done: acceptance criteria pass with evidence linked, code reviewed and merged by PR, tests pass, API docs and README updated, no secrets committed, integrated environment not broken, Jira updated. Story: As an eligible user, I want to reserve an available facility, so that I can use it at a set time. Given an eligible user and an available facility, when the user submits a valid reservation request, then the reservation is created with Pending status and is visible to the resource manager.

written.q: List the GitHub workflow rules for branching, pull requests, commits and releases.
written.a: Main is protected with no direct pushes; feature or fix branches named with the Jira key; each PR states purpose, linked Jira issue, evidence, tests and limitations and gets at least one meaningful peer review; commits are coherent and reference the Jira key; contribution quality matters more than commit count; CI builds and tests on every PR and failures are fixed before merge; at least one release-candidate tag and one final tag identify compatible versions; no secrets, synthetic data only.
